Separate exact derivative establishes SNR optimum precedes maximum mean signed chord. value.rationale: The primary Brownian gyrator experiment/model literature explicitly raises a choice of optimal discretization interval because very short and very long observations yield a weak circulation signal. This exact finite-chord theorem replaces an unsolved qualitative experimental choice with a unique computable lag, gives unexpected independence from temperature imbalance, and separates the optimum from both maximum raw signal and near-instability time scales. The logarithmic divergence near critical coupling is structurally motivated by the drift spectral gap. No claim of optimal total-record inference or of a paper-sized contribution is necessary to this concrete quantitative result.
